suggestions.title: Log Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights — three dark nights told your app the week was clean

rationale.science: At equal deficits, 5.5 vs 8.5 h sleep cut fat loss about 55% and raised lean-mass loss about 60% (Nedeltcheva 2010; Wang 2018). Sleep is the recovery account the eight new weekly sets are being charged to, so it is the one input that has to be measured this week rather than assumed.
rationale.data: sleep.nights stops at 8/6 (7.75 h). 8/7, 8/8 and 8/9 are all unlogged — three consecutive nights. Your 11-night mean is 6.8 h and the 7-night debt reads 1.8 h against the 7.5 h you set, and both numbers stopped updating on Thursday.
rationale.relationship: The debt flag is a three-night calendar mean, and it returns clean when three consecutive nights are missing. That is exactly what happened: every lift in Sunday's session carries debt: false, and this morning's WEEK IN REVIEW reports 'sleep 2/3 clean' off three logged nights in seven. A missing night does not make your app cautious, it makes it confident — and Sunday's session is the one carrying seven simultaneous changes that need an honest recovery read to be worth anything.

suggestions.predict: Log 8/7, 8/8 and 8/9 — estimates are fine, flag them as estimates — and log tonight. Grade on sleep.nights gaining entries for 8/7 through 8/10 within 24 hours, and on the next session's lastMeta.debt being computed from three real nights instead of three missing ones. If the nights go in and all three were 7 h or better, the clean flag was honest by accident and I will say so plainly.

suggestions.title: Set Sunday's five back by hand — your app recalled the proposals that made them, and there is no undo button

apply.to: Set back the five 8/9 volume additions by hand: hack 4 to 3, abs 4 to 3, curls 4 to 3, triceps 4 to 3, rows 3 to 2. Keep Friday's three (hams, chest, rear delt).

rationale.science: The largest dose-response analysis available (Pelland 2025, 67 studies, 2,058 participants) puts returns per set highest at 5-10 weekly sets and only intermediate at 11-18; 10 hard sets is the floor, not the target (Schoenfeld 2017). On a limited recovery budget the marginal set costs more than it buys.
rationale.data: This morning your app posted VOLUME PROPOSALS RECALLED — 'cold-start misfire: the ledger compared your first logged week against a week before this app existed' — and tightened the rule to 14 full days and two proposals on Sundays. The five sets it already shipped are still on the lifts: hack 4, abs 4, curls 4, triceps 4, rows 3. Friday's three were different and still stand — hams 4, chest 6, rear delt 6 were at or under the growth floor.
rationale.relationship: A recall stops future proposals, it does not reverse what already shipped. And I have to correct myself here: Friday's card said each of the five had a one-tap undo on file. They do not. The exUndo records exist for Friday's three OWNER'S CALL pushes and not for Sunday's five, which went in with no adjustment entry behind them. So this needs doing by hand, and my last card asked you to press a button that does not exist.

suggestions.predict: Set the five back and the next upper day gives attributable conversion reads on chest and rear delt — the two pushes that actually had an argument. Leave them and I expect at least two 'did not convert' verdicts inside a fortnight that neither of us can assign a cause to. Grade on entry counts: next upper day triceps 3 / curls 3 / rows 2, next lower day hack 3 / abs 3.

suggestions.title: Decide what press set four is — 250 has done its best work twice and banked neither time

apply.to: Before the next upper day, settle with your coach whether press set four is a fourth working set or an explicit lighter back-off — and log it as whichever it is

rationale.science: On a cut, defend load rather than chase volume, and take working sets to about 1-3 reps in reserve (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024; Grgic 2021). A trailing set that falls off a cliff is not a hard set, it is a scoring problem.
rationale.data: 8/6: press 250 x 8,8,7 drew PRESS — TARGET MET. 8/9: the same 250 x 8,8,7 plus a fourth set at 4 reps, opener rated at 1, and the feed carries no press row at all — while rows, triceps, sulek and lateral all got one from the same session. The variable that changed between the two is chest going 3 to 4 sets on 8/7.
rationale.relationship: My best read is that the target now has four slots, so a 4-rep fourth set fails it and the whole session scores as a miss. I could not verify that in your file — the target array is not saved with the session — so this is a best guess and I am labelling it as one. What is certain from the feed is that the best press in your record produced nothing on Sunday, and it is the second time in four days that 250 x 8,8,7 has gone unbanked.

suggestions.predict: Settle it and the next upper day produces a press row one way or the other — TARGET MET if set four is honestly reachable, or a clean miss you can actually read. Grade on whether any press feed row appears on the next upper day. If a row appears with four sets logged and no change to the load, my reading of the mechanism was wrong and I will withdraw it.
